faq.question: How much does window replacement cost in Dixon?
faq.answer: Dixon homeowners typically invest $4,000 to $9,000 for a full window replacement project. This small Solano County agricultural community features modest 1970s–2000s homes with standard window sizing. Projects covering 10–14 windows are typical. Single window installation starts at approximately $400.

faq.question: Do I need a permit to replace windows in Dixon?
faq.answer: Yes. Dixon requires a building permit for window replacements. Our team manages all permit applications with the City of Dixon Building Department on your behalf.

faq.question: Is it worth replacing 20-year-old windows in Dixon?
faq.answer: Often yes. Twenty-year-old windows in Dixon commonly show fogged glass, drafts and weak locks. Newer ENERGY STAR units improve comfort and curb appeal; Deluxe Windows compares payback against your utility rates and home style before recommending replacement.

faq.question: Should I choose fiberglass or vinyl windows in Dixon?
faq.answer: Vinyl is the value pick for most Dixon replacements and handles Bay Area weather well. Fiberglass (including Marvin Ultrex) is stronger, more stable in temperature swings and better for larger openings or coastal exposure. We show both side by side in the showroom and on-site.

faq.question: How long does window replacement take in Dixon?
faq.answer: Most Dixon projects are measured in one visit and installed in one to three working days once products arrive — typically four to eight weeks after ordering, depending on brand and custom sizes.
